articleBody:
- [ ] Measured total room perimeter and ceiling heights — Verifies whether standard upper cabinets fit or if custom height extensions and ceiling trim are required.
- [ ] Confirmed existing rough-in locations for water, drain, and gas — Establishes whether mechanical lines can stay put or need licensed sub-trade relocation.
- [ ] Checked dedicated electrical circuits and outlet placement — Ensures small appliance zones, dishwashers, and microwave drawers meet modern load demands without tripping breakers.
- [ ] Recorded manufacturer cut sheets for every planned appliance — Prevents building cabinet openings that choke ventilation or prevent refrigerator doors from opening fully.
- [ ] Marked 42-inch to 48-inch clearances along primary work paths — Keeps food prep zones comfortable and avoids tight bottlenecks between opposing island and perimeter counters.
- [ ] Reserved a 30 by 48 inch clear floor footprint at each station — Guarantees enough physical standing space in front of the sink, range, and refrigerator doors.
- [ ] Checked swing clearances for all opposing cabinet doors and pull-outs — Stops adjacent drawer fronts and decorative hardware from banging into each other across corners.
- [ ] Verified exterior venting paths for range hood exhaust ductwork — Confirms you can vent grease and moisture directly outside instead of blowing air back into the room.
- [ ] Identified load-bearing walls with a qualified framing contractor — Prevents structural sagging or costly delays before you commit to an open-concept island layout.
- [ ] Reviewed municipal permit requirements for plumbing and electrical updates — Ensures inspections go smoothly before dry-walling and cabinet installation begin.

How to use this checklist:
Walk through your existing kitchen with a tape measure, notepad, and this list before finalizing cabinet orders or hiring a contractor. Having these specific points checked ensures your quote covers all structural framing, sub-trades, and cabinetry adjustments accurately.
